title: Pretzel Bite Platter with Beer Cheese
displayTitle: Pretzel Bite Platter with Beer Cheese
seoTitle: Pretzel Bite Platter with Beer Cheese | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Soft pretzel bites and warm beer cheese dip for ten
subtitle: Soft pretzel bites and warm beer cheese dip for ten
description: Homemade or bakery pretzel bites are warmed until soft, served alongside a sharp beer cheese sauce and honey mustard. The platter is built for grazing while eyes stay on the screen.

steps.title: Make the beer cheese
steps.instruction: Melt cream cheese in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Whisk in cheddar gradually, then beer, Dijon, Worcestershire, and garlic powder until smooth and velvety.

steps.title: Hold the dip warm
steps.instruction: Transfer beer cheese to a slow cooker on warm or a double boiler setup. Stir every 10 minutes and add beer by the tablespoon if the sauce thickens too much.

steps.title: Warm pretzel bites
steps.instruction: Toss frozen pretzel bites with melted butter and coarse salt. Spread on sheet pans and bake at 400°F until heated through and lightly crisp at the edges, about 12–15 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Build the platter
steps.instruction: Pile warm pretzel bites on a large board with ramekins of beer cheese and honey mustard. Sprinkle extra coarse salt over the bites for that brewpub crunch.

steps.title: Serve and replenish
steps.instruction: Set out tongs and small plates. Replenish warm bites from the oven in batches so the platter never looks picked over during a long game.

proTips: Use sharp cheddar—mild cheese makes beer cheese taste flat and greasy.
A pinch of cornstarch whisked into cold beer prevents the sauce from breaking on hold.
Add pickled jalapeño slices to the beer cheese if the crew wants heat without extra dishes.
tonightSpread: Large pretzel board with beer cheese, honey mustard, and sliced pickles.
Slaw cups for crews who want crunch between salty, cheesy bites.
leftovers: Reheat beer cheese with beer over low heat—never microwave or it separates.
Turn extra bites into bread pudding with cheddar and scallions.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Dipping food keeps hands busy and conversation easy. Pretzel bites reheat without getting tough, and beer cheese feels like a treat even on a department budget.
mealPrepNotes: Beer cheese can be made ahead and reheated gently with a splash of beer. Pretzel bites from the freezer bake directly—do not thaw or they absorb moisture.

adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free bread/crust/wrapper alternative. Use a certified gluten-free beer or non-alcoholic broth instead. Use a certified gluten-free Worcestershire sauce.
